channel.title: The Local Europe - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Local Europe (thelocal.com)

item.title: '4-hour queues': Europe's airlines and airports fear summer travel chaos
item.description: Airlines across Europe have called on EU chiefs to review the ongoing roll-out for the EES biometric border checks amid fears the system will lead to border chaos this summer.

item.title: OPINION: Far-right Bardella is beatable in 2027, but no one looks capable of it
item.description: Marine Le Pen won't be the next president of France, but could her protégé Jordan Bardella win next year's race? Bardella has flaws, writes John Lichfield, but the problem is no one has yet emerged who looks capable of beating him.

item.title: 'Not a blank cheque': How the EU and US see Spain's mass migrant regularisation
item.description: Spain's mass migrant regularisation has caused fierce debate within the country, but media reports suggest the measure has now caught the attention of powers beyond the bloc.

item.title: Replacement for cash? How the new 'digital euro' would work for Europeans
item.description: Supporters say it would let Europeans make online payments without relying on US payment system, but critics fear it would allow governments to surveil citizens' payments. How would the digital euro work?

item.title: Switzerland announces June date for referendum on anti-immigration proposal
item.description: The Swiss government has decided to bring the right-wing initiative seeking to curb immigration to the ballot box on June 14th.

item.title: French court to rule on July 7th in Marine Le Pen appeal trial
item.description: A Paris appeals court said on Wednesday it will rule on July 7th in a fraud case against far-right leader Marine Le Pen, in what is expected to be a pivotal moment for French politics.

item.title: Hundreds of flights cancelled in Germany as Lufthansa staff strike
item.description: Germany's largest airline Lufthansa grounded flights on Thursday as a strike by pilots and cabin crew got underway.

item.title: 'Catastrophic effects': Why Germany is cutting integration courses for foreigners
item.description: Germany has confirmed plans to restrict access to integration courses, citing rising costs and a desire to focus spending on migrants likely to stay long term. Around 130,000 people could be affected – and the consequences could go much further.

item.title: Avalanche risk: How to stay safe skiing in the French Alps
item.description: As French ski resorts prepare for the peak February season, the news of more deaths have hit the headlines - here's how to stay safe while skiing in France.

item.title: 'A ritual shaped by an industry' - The rise of the pricey Paris proposals
item.description: It's long had a reputation as the city of romance, but now the French capital is supporting a growing number of businesses that will arrange an extravagant marriage proposal in a landmark setting - for a hefty fee, of course.
